articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft questions, latest intel, risers, CFB standouts
articles.description: Are the two Heisman-favorite quarterbacks rising the board? Is there a new WR2 in the class? Here's NFL draft spin off Week 2 of the CFB season.
articles.body:
The biggest storylines coming out of Week 3 of the 2026 college football season include Ole Miss defeating Lane Kiffin and LSU, Kentucky upsetting Texas A&M and Louisville winning a shootout with SMU.

But what about the top 2027 NFL draft prospects? Who stood out? Yes, the draft is still about seven months away, but our analysts are always looking down the road, taking early notes on top players and starting to stack their rankings for an exciting class.

With that in mind, Mel Kiper Jr. and Jordan Reid will size up CFB action through a draft-centric lens on Sundays all season long. They are answering lingering questions on the best 2027 prospects, sharing insights from scouts, picking out risers to watch and pulling back the curtain on their evaluation process. Here is what they saw and heard through Week 3.

Jump to:

Week 3 | Week 2

Sept. 20

Trinidad Chambliss and Darian Mensah are the current Heisman Trophy favorites. Has either QB played his way into the first round?

Reid: I do have Chambliss in Round 1 now, but I'm taking a wait-and-see approach with Mensah; Miami just hasn't played anyone yet.

Let's start with the 6-foot-3, 205-pound Mensah, whom I saw in person Friday when Miami faced Wake Forest. He started the game with an impressive 24 straight completions and finished 30-of-34 for 220 passing yards and three touchdowns. I saw real poise and command -- he seemed to be in full control of the offense during the first three quarters. I would classify his arm strength as slightly above average, as he has displayed beautiful touch down the field and enough velocity to drive the ball. The fourth quarter was the first time we saw him pressured and knocked off schedule this season, and the Hurricane's modest schedule so far brings curiosity. How will Mensah look against a higher quality opponent? Scouts already have Nov. 7 circled -- that's when Miami travels to Notre Dame. Mensah is certainly in the first-round conversation, but I want to see him against better competition.

Chambliss, meanwhile, went 33-of-48 for 363 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and one interception against LSU. Since taking over during the third game of last season, he has quickly become one of the most dynamic signal-callers in the country. His size (6-foot, 205 pounds) and age (will be a 25-year-old NFL rookie) will be major talking points, but his entire career has been about defying the odds. What gives me confidence about his next-level projection? How he elevates his play in big games and how efficiently he attacks the middle of the field. That second part is the worry with shorter passers, but Chambliss threw strike after strike Saturday night. His measurables won't be for everyone, but Russell Wilson is the NFL comparison that I use for him. If the current trend continues, I believe a team will take him in Round 1.

What is one shift on your board you didn't expect to make this early?

articles.headline: Reds place ace Chase Burns on 15-day IL with groin strain
articles.description: The Reds have placed right-hander Chase Burns on the 15-day injured list with a right groin strain. A first-time All-Star this season, the 23-year-old went 15-3 with a 2.86 ERA.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- The Reds placed right-hander Chase Burns on the 15-day injured list Sunday with a right groin strain, ending the All-Star's season.

"After his start [Friday], he just came in ... and he felt the right groin a little bit," Reds manager Terry Francona said. "So again, we're being very cautious."

The move to the IL was retroactive to Saturday.

Burns, 23, has pitched 154⅓ innings this season, far surpassing his 43⅓ innings during his rookie season in 2025. He is 15-3 with a 2.86 ERA, 185 strikeouts and a 1.166 WHIP in 29 starts.

His 238 strikeouts through his first 36 career starts rank third in Reds franchise history since 1900.

Burns had worked three innings in each of his past three starts to limit his innings for the remainder of the season.

"He did a really, really good job," Francona said. "I think it makes sense to not push him for [another] three-inning start. We got him to a point where next year, however he pitches, it's not going to be determined by, 'Oh, we've got to be careful with this.' So that's a really good thing."

Burns was named to the National League All-Star squad but did not pitch because of a groin issue.

"Not how I wanted it to end," Burns said. "Both groins kind of got upset this year. Kind of frustrating. Happy with the way the season went, just the growth and experience. Ready to get back next year. I'm excited."

In corresponding roster moves Sunday, the Reds selected right-hander Carson Spiers from Triple-A Louisville and designated outfielder TJ Friedl for assignment.

Friedl batted .172 with four homers and 13 RBIs in 91 games. He was optioned to Louisville on Friday for the second time this season.

articles.headline: Raptors honor Kyle Lowry with golden 'GROAT' statue
articles.description: Lowry also received a key to the city of Toronto and a special dinner to honor his contribution to the franchise.
articles.body:
With a sea of red, white and black Kyle Lowry jerseys filling the streets of Toronto for an honorary block party, the guard's legacy will forever be stamped in the city's lore with an exclusive commemorative figure.

On Saturday, the Toronto Raptors honored Lowry's career with a block party outside of Scotiabank Arena, unveiling a golden raptor statue. The sculpture features Lowry's No. 7 jersey while dribbling a basketball and stands on a nameplate that reads "The Greatest Raptor of All Time. Kyle Lowry | 2012-2021, 2026."

The statue unveiling follows the franchise's August announcement that it would retire Lowry's jersey number during the upcoming 2026-27 season. It will be raised to the rafters at the conclusion of Toronto's home matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers on Jan. 10.

Along with the statue, the six-time All-Star received a key to the city.

"I've been looking forward to this moment for years. I always said that Toronto is home, and that I'd retire a Raptor, and to see my No. 7 go up in that building is going to mean everything to me," Lowry said. "We built something special here -- my teammates, the organization, the city and the fans, and all of Canada. We became champions together, and to be able to share this night with all of them, and with my family, is going to mean a lot to me."

Lowry, who spent nine of his 20 seasons in Toronto, helped bring the Raptors their only NBA championship in the 2019 NBA Finals. He will also join Basketball Hall of Famer Vince Carter as the only Raptors to have their numbers retired -- Carter's was retired in November 2024.

The 40-year-old Lowry announced his retirement in July after signing a one-day contract with Toronto to retire as a member of the franchise.

He averaged 13.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and six assists in his 20 seasons.

articles.headline: Ernie Accorsi, longtime NFL executive and Giants GM, dies at 84
articles.description: Longtime NFL executive Ernie Accorsi, the architect of the Giants team that pulled off one of the biggest upsets in Super Bowl history, has died. He was 84.
articles.body:
Longtime NFL executive Ernie Accorsi, the architect of the New York Giants team that pulled off one of the biggest upsets in Super Bowl history, has died. He was 84.

The Giants announced Sunday that Accorsi died Saturday, surrounded by his family.

"Ernie helped shape the course of New York Giants history through his vision, leadership and unwavering belief in building a championship organization," Giants owner John Mara said in a statement. "Beyond his accomplishments as a football executive, he was a trusted advisor and dear friend. His legacy will forever be part of the Giants, and he will be greatly missed."

"Ernie Accorsi was one of the most respected football minds in NFL history and a dear friend whose wisdom and perspective I valued tremendously," NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement. "Throughout his remarkable career, he shaped championship-caliber clubs and earned the admiration of everyone who worked with him."

Accorsi spent parts of four decades in top front-office roles around the NFL and served as general manager for three different teams, most recently the Giants from 1998 to 2006.

Accorsi served as the GM of the Cleveland Browns from 1985 to 1992 before joining the Giants as their assistant GM in 1994, working under Hall of Fame executive George Young. He replaced Young as the GM four years later and built the core of a team that reached three Super Bowls and won two Lombardi Trophies.

Under Accorsi, the Giants hired two-time Super Bowl-winning coach Tom Coughlin in 2004 and pulled off the draft day trade for star quarterback Eli Manning later that year.

"Ernie will always be remembered, and I say this out of great respect -- he's the guy that made the trade for Eli Manning," Coughlin said in a statement released by the Giants. "That will go down in Giants history as one of the great moves of all time. Was it risky? Sure it was risky. Ernie did it. Shut the door, went in, he did it on his own. It was his move."

Accorsi also drafted multiple other franchise icons, including Osi Umenyiora, Justin Tuck, Chris Snee and Brandon Jacobs.

"I know he was the believer in me and kind of the reason I got here," Manning said in a statement. "I appreciated him so much for building such great teams and giving us the opportunity to win some championships here."

Accorsi retired as Giants GM in 2006, one year before New York upset the then-undefeated New England Patriots in Super Bowl XLII. The Giants beat the Patriots again four years later in Super Bowl XLVI.

A graduate of Wake Forest, Accorsi also served as GM of the then-Baltimore Colts from 1982 to 1983.

"He was always so fun to sit with and just talk, whether it's the Giants or his time in Baltimore around the Colts," Manning said. "His stories around the NFL and the people he was around that shaped his career were always so entertaining. I know the Giants organization owes a lot of thanks to Ernie Accorsi and what he was able to do for the organization."

articles.headline: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by Baker Mayfield and Justin Jefferson
articles.description: Rounding up all top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
articles.body:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

An animated discussion among the Cincinnati Bengals' defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

The source was cornerback DJ Turner II's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

"I'm always about that action," Turner said. "I gotta put it on."

Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king.

To kick off Week 2, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb arrived in a plaid Archival button-down shirt paired with dark denim jeans.

Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

Sunday afternoon arrivals

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield was dressed to impress, arriving for a home game against his former team, the Cleveland Browns. Mayfield wore a cream polo with khaki and green striped pants and white shoes.

Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson wore a red letterman jacket and loose-fit khaki pants ahead of a road matchup against the Chicago Bears.

articles.headline: Has Isak finally found form at Liverpool? Winner at Bournemouth gives Iraola hope
articles.description: Liverpool's expensively assembled attack had looked devoid of a spark at Bournemouth, with Alexander Isak virtually anonymous ... until he wasn't.
articles.body:
BOURNEMOUTH, England -- As Liverpool striker Alexander Isak watched his mishit cross veer erratically out of play at AFC Bournemouth's Vitality Stadium, ironic jeers rained down on him from the stands.

Minutes later, the Sweden international was the subject of adulation -- not ire -- from the away section of the crowd after netting what turned out to be the winning goal in his side's hard-fought 1-0 Premier League victory.

- Premier League VAR review: Was Rice lucky not to be sent off?

- First-month grades for all 20 Premier League teams: From an A+ to F

- Ranking the hottest men's teams right now: Can anyone stop Barcelona?

The sequence was a microcosm of the life of a striker and a timely reminder of why the Reds broke the British transfer record to sign Isak from Newcastle United little more than 12 months ago.

Up until that point, it had largely been a drab, laborious slog for Andoni Iraola's side on their head coach's return to his former club. The Reds' expensively assembled attack had looked devoid of a spark, with Isak virtually anonymous at the Vitality Stadium ... until he wasn't.

With the clock ticking towards the hour mark, Cody Gakpo's cross bobbled into the path of the forward, who finished with aplomb before charging towards the elated away end. The hearty embrace he received from the visiting supporters felt symbolic. After the most turbulent of debut seasons, there can now be no doubting that Isak is a Liverpool player.

"A striker's job is like this," Iraola said in his postmatch news conference. "He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control but in the end he has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition's half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals."

Indeed, Isak's tally of four Premier League goals has already exceeded his haul from the entirety of last term (three). In the 81 minutes he played against Bournemouth, the 26-year-old had 34 touches and completed just 11 of his 16 attempted passes. Ultimately, though, it is immaterial what he does outside of the penalty area if he can continue showing the kind of proficiency that has characterised the early weeks of his season.

Of course, the fact that Isak was given the platform to go on and win the game owed much to the robustness of Liverpool's defence. For the first time since the beginning of Arne Slot's tenure in August/September 2024, the Reds have kept three consecutive clean sheets in the Premier League, with summer signing Jérémy Jacquet impressing once again on the south coast.

At the end of a week that saw him earn his first senior callup to the France national team, the 21-year-old continued his outstanding start at the heart of Liverpool's back line. articles.headline: Jonathan David steers Atlético Madrid past 10-man Real Madrid
articles.description: Second-half goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David gave Atlético Madrid a 2-1 victory over 10-man Real Madrid at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
articles.body:
Second-half goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David gave Atlético Madrid a 2-1 victory over 10-man Real Madrid at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Victory for Atlético helped them climb above their local rivals and condemned Jose Mourinho's side to a second defeat of the season from their opening seven games.

It was a cagey first period but the turning point came after the break when Dean Huijsen gave away a penalty and was sent off before Grimaldo tucked away the resulting penalty for his second goal since joining from Bayer Leverkusen this summer.

David carried on his fine goalscoring form and made it three goals in his last three games by doubling Atlético's advantage.

Antonio Rüdiger breathed life into the contest late on but it was too little, too late for Mourinho who suffered defeat in his first meeting with Diego Simeone since 2014.

The result already leaves Real six points behind 100% Barcelona and they have been leapfrogged by Atlético who are now a point in front of their same-city neighbours.

After a slow start, the game quickly opened up. Atletico's first proper chance came from Giuliano Simeone, who capitalised on some messy defending but fired wide of the target.

Atletico were growing into the game and Los Blancos were caught sleeping once again which handed an opportunity to the hosts but David Hancko and Lee Kang-in both had efforts blocked.

Real Madrid landed the first shot on target of the contest in the 40th minute, when Arda Guler tried his luck from distance, which needed to be tipped over.

Atletico troubled Thibaut Courtois for the first time just two minutes after the break when Alex Baena tried his luck from range but the Belgium goalkeeper pushed it away.

The game changed when Huijsen brought down Simeone inside the area which led to a penalty and the Spanish defender saw red which forced Real Madrid to play the majority of the half with a man less before Grimaldo slotted his spot-kick away to make it 1-0.

Atletico were looking to increase their lead and Lee was the next player to test Courtois, but he was able to make the save.

They soon made it two when David poked home from Simeone's cross just before Julian Alvarez was brought into the game.

The hosts should have been three up when but Romero saw his header stopped by Courtois from a corner before Ibrahima Konate was on hand to deny Alvarez on the goal-line.

The visitors had a chance to pull one back out of nowhere on the counter through Yan Diomande but saw his one-on-one effort pushed out by Jan Oblak.

The noise inside the Metropolitano dropped when Rudiger headed home from Bernardo Silva's set-piece but it was too late as Atletico hung on for the points.
